items.title: Cursor ships the Agent SDK — build and deploy custom agents as code
items.summary: An agent is now a folder: instructions.md holds the prompt, tools/ defines typed actions, skills/ holds procedures loaded on demand, mcp-connections/ adds MCP tools, channels/ wires up triggers (GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket PR and CI events, Slack, webhooks, cron). CLI commands scaffold (init), run locally with a playground (dev), test with evals that assert on tool calls and reply shape (eval, github replay <pr-url> to turn a real PR into test fixtures), and ship (deploy) to Cursor-hosted infra with a URL, logs, and a dashboard for secrets. GA as of Oct 20.
items.why: Building a custom coding or review agent is now a scaffold-test-deploy CLI workflow with real evals, not a bespoke infra project.
items.action: Run npx @cursor/agent-sdk init with the PR-autofixer template, then agent-sdk github replay against one of your own merged PRs to see how the agent would have acted on it.

items.title: OpenAI ships GPT-6.1 Terra — a cheap, 1M-context model built for computer use and visual reasoning
items.summary: gpt-6.1-terra takes text and image input (no audio/video), has a 1.05M-token context window and up to 128K output tokens, and supports tool calling (web search, file search, code interpreter, computer use, MCP) through the Responses API. Pricing: $1/M input, $0.05/M cached input, $5/M output.
items.why: A model this cheap with a 1M-token window and native computer-use tool support makes running an agent against a GUI while holding a huge context a cost a routine pipeline step can actually absorb, not just a demo.
items.action: Point one image-heavy or computer-use step in your pipeline at gpt-6.1-terra and compare cost/latency against whatever Sol- or Astra-tier model you're using today.

eval.reason: New model tier confirmed on OpenAI's own changelog (Oct 26) and model page; distinct from previously covered GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra; not a duplicate.
